operations.evidence: Charge or summons outcomes for non-victim-based offences took a median of 40 days.
Processing time does not represent parcel-level public-safety conditions.
Drug offence charge or summons outcomes took 53 days, down from 62 days.
Drug offence volumes and outcomes are highly influenced by enforcement activity.
Possession of weapons charge or summons outcomes took 18 days, down from 22 days.
This outcome timing does not locate offences or quantify local exposure.
Public order charge or summons outcomes took 28 days, down from 36 days.
Changes can reflect operational and case-mix effects.
Around 12.9% of offences involving a firearm resulted in a charge or summons, up from 12.0%.
Firearm involvement is a cross-cutting subset and the rate is not a local risk score.
Around 13.0% of knife-enabled offences resulted in a charge or summons, up from 11.5%.
Knife-enabled outcomes must not be interpreted as exact-location evidence.
The knife-enabled charge or summons rate of 13.0% was higher than the 7.5% rate for equivalent offences not involving a knife.
Differences may reflect offence seriousness, evidence, and investigation selection.
The bulletin covers all territorial police forces in England and Wales and British Transport Police.
National coverage does not guarantee uniform recording quality across forces.
The current crime outcomes framework was introduced in April 2013, replacing the narrower detections framework.
Long-term comparisons across framework changes require caution.
The main outcomes data are a snapshot of the case status of offences recorded during the year ending March 2026.
Cases still open at the snapshot date can change outcome later.
40 source rows and 84 operation rows were prepared for line-by-line website visibility.
